source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Use a wrong user account to log in web UI
2. Use correct admin accounts  to log in web UI
3. Log out from web UI

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Should NOT log in with wrong user account
2. Should be logged in with correct admin accounts of different privileges successfully
3. Should be back to login page after logout

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- "Login with Domain Name": log in via the BMC Domain Name (FQDN). Agent can resolve the FQDN and load the login page; DNS/domain must be configured.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the page/login result reached via the domain name so user confirms domain-name login works.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: none; depends on BMC DNS/domain being configured.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL reasonably interprets `Domain Name` as the BMC FQDN and identifies DNS/browser dependencies, but it supplies no authoritative resolver, A/AAAA/CNAME chain, certificate/SNI/Host binding, cache/proxy controls, account attempt limits or proof that logout invalidates the session; `risk: none` is unsafe for credential-bearing access.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly adds controlled DNS, certificate SAN/identity correlation, protected accounts, bounded failures and session invalidation. This review retains that classification and makes the FQDN path itself a non-substitutable checkpoint.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 844/2291 preserves PARTIAL but incorrectly locates the browser path at a DUT host over SSH and repeats the FQDN assumption without validating DNS/TLS/account/session evidence.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1007 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 treats Project FQDN, resolver, accounts and certificate inputs as readiness rather than permanent blockage; ED-35 preserves the domain-name access route and coverage difference from IP access; ED-38 requires protected credentials, bounded execution, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Use the Project-approved BMC domain name/FQDN—not a substituted raw IP—to reach the intended BMC web service, reject one bounded invalid account, authenticate the approved administrator privilege matrix and then return to login with the authenticated session invalidated.
original_method: Resolve the approved FQDN through the authoritative Project DNS view, record the complete answer chain, bind every accepted address to the intended BMC and certificate SAN, open the web UI with the FQDN preserved as the HTTPS authority, execute the bounded wrong/correct account cases and verify logout plus old-session rejection.
manual_activity: An engineer supplies and approves the FQDN, authoritative DNS view, expected address/certificate identity and disposable account matrix with attempt limits. After confirmation, browser automation can perform resolution, identity binding and login/logout checks; the engineer owns any DNS exception and final verdict.
required_inputs: Canonical BMC FQDN with case/trailing-dot/IDN expectations if applicable, authoritative zone/records and approved recursive resolver or split-horizon view
Expected A/AAAA and any CNAME chain, TTL, DNSSEC or Project integrity expectation, IPv4/IPv6 selection and negative/alternate-view behavior
Exact BMC management IP/MAC/serial/firmware and TLS certificate SAN/issuer/fingerprint/chain expected for that FQDN
Browser/version, trusted CA, proxy/no-proxy, DNS-over-HTTPS policy, local resolver/cache state, redirects and requirement that the address bar/Host/SNI remain the FQDN
Disposable wrong credential plus each approved administrator account/privilege, MFA/CAPTCHA/SSO behavior, lockout/rate-limit threshold and maximum attempts
Protected secret/session handling, expected logout/token invalidation, BMC audit event, alternate OOB recovery and cleanup
safety_requirements: Do not authenticate until the FQDN's approved resolver view, complete answer set, certificate SAN/chain and BMC identity all agree. A familiar login page is not identity proof.
Do not use `-k`, ignore browser certificate warnings, disable hostname validation or substitute the raw IP; those actions remove the domain-name/TLS coverage that distinguishes this case.

Control proxies, browser secure-DNS settings and caches so a proxy response, stale entry or temporary hosts override cannot silently satisfy the test; record any explicitly approved override as different coverage.
If multiple A/AAAA answers are valid, bind and test each required Project endpoint or record untested addresses; never choose one silently.

Use only protected disposable/approved accounts and one bounded invalid attempt within lockout/alarm limits. Do not expose credentials, cookies, tokens, FQDN-associated customer data or privileged pages.

Verify the logged-in identity and assigned privilege, but do not broaden this case into destructive administration. After logout, test controlled reuse of the prior token/cookie rather than accepting a redirect alone.

Do not clear dmesg, syslog, SEL, DNS or BMC audit logs. Do not automatically retry resolution/authentication after unexpected answers, certificate mismatch, wrong target, lockout warning or session-cleanup failure.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, query the canonical FQDN through the approved resolver/view, record A/AAAA/CNAME/TTL and resolver metadata, compare with the expected network map and validate certificate SAN/chain plus BMC firmware/serial identity without credentials.

After approval, open the validated FQDN in an isolated supported browser with controlled proxy/cache settings and prove the request authority remains the domain name rather than being replaced by a raw IP or unrelated redirect.
Run exactly the approved invalid attempt, then each named administrator privilege case; capture redacted authenticated identity/privilege and minimal expected landing/access evidence.

Log out each test session, verify return to login and rejection of the prior session on a protected resource; reconcile sessions/accounts, collect security events and report facts without retries or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the canonical FQDN, resolver/view, complete address and certificate/BMC identity map, proxy/cache behavior and required IP-family coverage.
Approve disposable account/privilege matrix, one invalid attempt, MFA/lockout handling, session reuse check and recovery.
Adjudicate DNS/TLS deviations or untested address records, review authentication/logout evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: FQDN resolution and browser load fit the title, but the prose is incomplete: it does not prove authoritative DNS results, preserve FQDN/SNI/Host coverage, validate TLS/BMC identity, bound account attempts or verify session invalidation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved resolver diagnostic and a trusted browser. Capture the canonical DNS answer/TTL chain, validate every required address and certificate SAN against the exact BMC, preserve FQDN authority, then execute the bounded account/logout matrix with protected secrets and session-reuse evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Domain-name login title, wrong/correct-admin/logout body, no Script and 5/0-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Authoritative DNS and cache/proxy preflight; complete answer-to-BMC-to-certificate binding; browser access with FQDN authority preserved; bounded wrong/approved-admin matrix; logout-token invalidation and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BMC web service, Project DNS view, certificate deployment and supported account provider.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/UI build, DNS zone/record revision, resolver, certificate chain/fingerprint and browser/version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project DNS/IP allocation, BMC certificate and web account/session specifications.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the title's domain-name route observable and safe while retaining the generic login/logout steps as separate downstream checkpoints.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Raw-IP login does not test FQDN resolution, Host/SNI routing or SAN validation; DNS success alone does not prove BMC identity or authentication; a login redirect does not prove logout invalidation; one address does not cover a required multi-address record set.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: FQDN/DNS view, address/identity/certificate map, browser network behavior, accounts, attempt limits, sessions and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Poisoned/stale/split DNS, proxy interception or certificate mismatch can expose admin credentials to the wrong endpoint; invalid attempts can trigger lockout.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may define an alternate resolver, private CA, split-horizon record or controlled temporary mapping, but must record original domain-name method, actual DNS/transport path, reason, approval and coverage. Direct raw-IP access or disabled hostname validation is not equivalent and leaves FQDN/TLS coverage unverified.
expected_evidence: Canonical FQDN, authoritative/recursive resolver identity and timestamped A/AAAA/CNAME/TTL answer chain from the approved DNS view
Expected-versus-observed IP set and independent correlation to BMC MAC/serial/firmware plus certificate SAN/issuer/fingerprint/chain
Browser/version, CA trust, proxy/no-proxy, secure-DNS/cache state and proof the HTTPS authority/Host/SNI remains the FQDN across redirects
Bounded invalid-login rejection without lockout and redacted login identity/privilege evidence for every approved admin account
Logout return plus failed reuse of each prior session on protected content, BMC security/audit events, cleanup/recovery and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Items title supplies the domain-name access route and the Procedure/Criteria supply the downstream authentication/logout matrix. Although the body omits the FQDN details, the conventional BMC web meaning is sufficiently identifiable and Project DNS parameters can complete it without choosing among irreconcilable operations.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The FQDN resolution, identity-bound HTTPS access and account/session checks are understandable. The exact name, DNS view, certificate, accounts and limits are supplyable execution inputs, so they require package/user confirmation rather than a permanent semantic block.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its FQDN/DNS interpretation but rejects `risk: none` and adds authoritative answers, certificate/BMC binding, protected account limits and logout-token evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation and its DNS/TLS/proxy/cache/account safeguards; adds explicit FQDN authority preservation, multi-address coverage and raw-IP non-equivalence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Corrects the location from DUT-host/SSH to the DNS/TLS/browser path and replaces deferred runtime checking with a complete name-to-identity-to-session evidence chain.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents cached, proxied, certificate-invalid or raw-IP access—and a mere login redirect—from being reported as successful domain-name-bound BMC authentication and logout.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike the preceding undefined MAC case, a BMC domain name supplies a conventional web endpoint semantics that Project DNS data can instantiate. The unique coverage is not just account login: DNS must yield the approved address set, HTTPS must authenticate the same FQDN/BMC and the browser must actually use that authority. Only after that chain is proven can the generic account/logout body satisfy the source.
